skill.name: azure-resource-manager-cosmosdb-dotnet
skill.description: Guides use of Azure.ResourceManager.CosmosDB for .NET management plane tasks, including Cosmos DB account provisioning, SQL databases, containers, throughput, RBAC, and ARM resource navigation.
skill.summary: Use Azure.ResourceManager.CosmosDB in .NET to provision and manage Cosmos DB resources through Azure Resource Manager.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Static external-command alerts are false positives caused by markdown code fences and inline API names, not executable backticks. The Azure credential environment variable alerts are documentation placeholders with no credential values. I found one semantic high-risk issue: the skill demonstrates printing Cosmos DB keys and connection strings to console output.

remediation.issue: Cosmos DB keys and connection strings are printed in the example.
remediation.suggestion: Replace console output with redacted placeholders and explain that keys and connection strings must not be logged. Prefer Key Vault or managed identity guidance for secret handling.

remediation.issue: Service principal credential placeholders need stronger safety guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Add a note to prefer managed identity or workload identity when possible. Warn users not to commit environment files or paste secrets into prompts.

semantic_findings.title: Credential Values Printed To Console
semantic_findings.description: The Get Connection Information example retrieves Cosmos DB account keys and connection strings, then writes the primary key and each connection string to console output. This can expose production credentials in terminal history, build logs, or AI transcripts.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example explicitly calls GetKeysAsync and GetConnectionStringsAsync and prints secret values. This is a clear credential disclosure risk even though it is documentation.

content.value_statement: Cosmos DB management code often mixes data plane and management plane APIs. This skill guides .NET developers through Azure Resource Manager patterns for accounts, databases, containers, throughput, and credentials.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use Azure.ResourceManager.CosmosDB instead of Microsoft.Azure.Cosmos.
Shows ARM authentication with DefaultAzureCredential and subscription resource access.
Outlines account, SQL database, and SQL container creation workflows.
Covers manual and autoscale throughput configuration patterns.
Lists key resource classes and reference files for deeper topics.
limitations: Does not implement document CRUD, queries, stored procedures, or data plane operations.
Examples require valid Azure permissions and an existing resource group.
Version notes may become outdated as the Azure SDK changes.
Security guidance should be updated before using key or connection string examples.

use_cases.title: Create Cosmos DB Infrastructure
use_cases.description: Plan .NET ARM code that provisions Cosmos DB accounts, SQL databases, containers, and throughput settings.

use_cases.title: Review SDK Boundaries
use_cases.description: Confirm whether a task belongs to the management plane SDK or the data plane Cosmos SDK.

use_cases.title: Add Throughput Automation
use_cases.description: Design safe manual or autoscale throughput updates for Cosmos DB SQL databases and containers.

prompt_templates.title: Choose The Right SDK
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning a Cosmos DB task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to decide whether my task needs Azure.ResourceManager.CosmosDB or Microsoft.Azure.Cosmos. My task is: [describe task].

prompt_templates.title: Plan Resource Provisioning
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate user creating new Azure resources.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline the management plane steps for creating a Cosmos DB account, SQL database, and SQL container in .NET.

prompt_templates.title: Design Throughput Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to compare manual throughput and autoscale throughput for my Cosmos DB workload, then recommend a .NET ARM update flow.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Automation Safety
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my Cosmos DB management plan for credential exposure, least privilege, idempotency, and long-running operation handling.

output_examples.input: I need a Cosmos DB account and SQL container with autoscale throughput.
output: Use the management plane SDK because the task creates Azure resources.
Create or get the resource group, define the account, then create the SQL database and container.
Apply autoscale throughput after the database or container exists, and wait for required operations to complete.

output_examples.input: I need to insert documents and run SQL queries against Cosmos DB.
output_examples.output: Use Microsoft.Azure.Cosmos for document CRUD and queries. Azure.ResourceManager.CosmosDB is for account, database, container, throughput, and RBAC management.

output_examples.input: Review my credential handling plan for Cosmos DB provisioning.
output: Use DefaultAzureCredential with managed identity when possible.
Avoid printing keys, connection strings, tenant IDs, client IDs, or client secrets.
Store any required secrets in a managed secret store and redact them from logs.

best_practices: Prefer managed identity or DefaultAzureCredential and grant least privilege Azure roles.
Keep management plane and data plane operations in separate services or modules.
Redact keys, connection strings, subscription IDs, and tenant IDs from logs and prompts.
anti_patterns: Using Azure.ResourceManager.CosmosDB for document reads, writes, or SQL queries.
Printing account keys or connection strings while testing provisioning flows.
Hardcoding resource names, regions, credentials, or throughput values without configuration review.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps with .NET management plane work for Azure Cosmos DB resources through Azure Resource Manager.

faq.question: Does it replace Microsoft.Azure.Cosmos?
faq.answer: No. Use Microsoft.Azure.Cosmos for document CRUD, queries, stored procedures, triggers, and data plane operations.

faq.question: Can it help create Cosmos DB accounts?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes account, SQL database, SQL container, and throughput management workflows.

faq.question: Does it require Azure credentials?
faq.answer: Yes. Examples assume Azure authentication through DefaultAzureCredential and suitable Azure role permissions.

faq.question: Is it safe to print connection strings?
faq.answer: No. Keys and connection strings are secrets and should be redacted from terminals, logs, and prompts.
